input.quote: 9.4 Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form without cause by delivering the written notice specified in Section 29.4. Customer owes only accrued Fees, and Vendor shall refund prepaid Fees for the period after termination.
input.rationale: Section 9.4 gives us an unconditional right to terminate the Agreement or any Order Form without cause, and Section 29.4 fixes that notice period at thirty days — our preferred 30-day convenience right. Termination carries no penalty or early-termination fee (we owe only accrued Fees), and Vendor must refund prepaid Fees for the post-termination period (reinforced by Section 10.2). Vendor is given no convenience right anywhere: Section 9 limits Vendor to material breach (9.1) and insolvency (9.2), Section 20.5 lets Vendor terminate only an infringing item, and Section 24.4 bars termination on our change of control, so Vendor cannot walk away during the three-year term (Section 8.1). Section 7.7's liquidated damages attach to late invoice payment, not to termination, so they are not an early-termination fee under this rule (addressed separately under the liquidated-damages rule). The clause meets the preferred position; no redline proposed.
